answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit — a quartz-hard bond — before it can trade or vote. Like a lantern that only lights for those who carry real fuel, the stake makes spawning thousands of fake identities expensive. Reputation then accrues slowly, the way a sparrow earns trust by returning to the same nest each season, so fresh accounts cannot instantly outvote honest ones. Attackers pay real cost per identity while honest agents keep working.
